skill.name: documentation-writer
skill.description: Helps write software documentation using the Diataxis framework, with clear separation between tutorials, how-to guides, reference, and explanation documents.
skill.summary: Creates structured Markdown documentation using the Diataxis framework.
skill.author: github

security_audit.summary: The only static finding is a hardcoded URL in SKILL.md line 9. It is a documentation framework citation in a prompt-only skill, and no prompt injection, exfiltration intent, or executable behavior was found.

static_findings.snippet: Your work is strictly guided by the principles and structure of the Diátaxis Framework (https://diat

finding_verdicts.reason: The URL on SKILL.md line 9 is a citation to the Diataxis framework inside prompt text, not executable network behavior. SKILL.md line 45 also tells the assistant not to consult external sources unless the user provides a link and instructs it to do so.

content.value_statement: Teams often mix tutorials, guides, reference, and explanations. This skill structures documentation with the Diataxis framework and writes clear Markdown.
actual_capabilities: Classifies documentation requests as tutorials, how-to guides, reference, or explanation content.
Asks for audience, goal, scope, and exclusions before drafting.
Proposes a table of contents before writing the full document.
Writes well-formatted Markdown after the outline is approved.
Uses provided Markdown files to match project tone and terminology.
Avoids copying source material unless the user explicitly asks.
limitations: It requires user input before it can choose the best document type.
It waits for outline approval before producing the full document.
It does not consult external websites unless the user provides a link and instructions.
It depends on the accuracy and completeness of the project context supplied by the user.

use_cases.title: Plan New Developer Documentation
use_cases.description: Create a clear outline for a new tutorial, guide, reference page, or explanation before drafting.

use_cases.title: Improve Existing Markdown Docs
use_cases.description: Use existing Markdown files as context to match tone, terminology, and structure across a documentation set.

use_cases.title: Separate Mixed Documentation
use_cases.description: Turn unclear documentation requests into the correct Diataxis document type with a focused scope.

prompt_templates.title: Classify My Documentation Request
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request to choose the right Diataxis document type.
prompt_templates.prompt: I need documentation for [feature or product]. Ask me the questions needed to classify it as a tutorial, how-to guide, reference, or explanation.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Outline
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request after audience and goal are known.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Diataxis-based outline for [document type]. The audience is [audience], the goal is [goal], and the scope is [scope]. Exclude [exclusions].

prompt_templates.title: Draft Approved Documentation
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request to write content from an approved outline.
prompt_templates.prompt: Write the full Markdown document from this approved outline: [outline]. Use clear language and keep the content focused on [audience] achieving [goal].

prompt_templates.title: Align With Existing Docs
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request using repository documentation as style context.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use these Markdown files as context for tone, terminology, and structure: [files]. Create a [document type] for [topic], but do not copy source text unless requested.

output_examples.input: Write docs for a first-time setup flow.
output_examples.output: The skill asks for the target audience, desired outcome, scope, and exclusions. It then proposes a tutorial outline with setup steps, checks, and next steps.

output_examples.input: Document every option for a command-line tool.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies this as reference documentation and drafts a structured Markdown page with command purpose, options, defaults, and usage notes.

output_examples.input: Explain why the project uses a queue for background work.
output_examples.output: The skill treats the request as explanation content and produces a concept-focused outline covering context, tradeoffs, and design reasoning.

best_practices: Provide the target audience, document goal, scope, and exclusions before asking for a draft.
Approve or revise the proposed outline before requesting the full Markdown content.
Share representative Markdown files when you need the output to match an existing documentation style.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for one document to serve as tutorial, guide, reference, and explanation at the same time.
Do not skip audience and goal details when the document needs practical steps.
Do not ask it to copy existing documentation unless you have permission and explicitly need copied text.

faq.question: What documentation framework does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses the Diataxis framework to separate tutorials, how-to guides, reference, and explanation content.

faq.question: Can it write the full document immediately?
faq.answer: It is designed to ask clarifying questions and propose an outline before drafting the full document.

faq.question: Can it use existing project documentation?
faq.answer: Yes. It can use provided Markdown files to understand tone, terminology, and structure.

faq.question: Will it copy text from existing files?
faq.answer: No. The skill says not to copy from provided Markdown files unless the user explicitly asks.

faq.question: Does it browse external websites?
faq.answer: No. It should only consult external sources when the user provides a link and instructs it to do so.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
